title_vi: Linux khởi động chậm ở đâu? Đo và đọc bằng systemd-analyze và journalctl

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body independently hashed as Git blob; computed OID matches the source map. Non-empty source was read; no source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Bài kia kể tám bước khởi động Linux và đọc tĩnh các tệp đơn vị systemd; bài này dạy đo và đọc thời gian khởi động, không lặp lại các bước.

claims.reason: systemd-analyze and journalctl manual pages read at the pinned systemd commit; the arithmetic on the manual's example was run by the author; no real boot was measured because the authoring machine is a container

mobile.reason: figure text measured arithmetically by scripts.figures check; no whole-lesson render at 320, 375 and 430 px recorded

claims.claim_vi: systemd-analyze time prints the time spent in the kernel before userspace, in the initrd, and in normal userspace; the manual's example on a real machine is 2.584s (kernel) + 19.176s (initrd) + 47.847s (userspace) = 1min 9.608s; the numbers are measured up to the point where all services have been spawned, not until they finished initialization.
claims.verified_by: Read from the pinned commit; the file hash was compared.

claims.claim_vi: systemd-analyze blame lists units by initialization time, with caveats (a slow unit may be waiting for another; Type=simple services are not shown; only the activating state is timed; it reflects program code more than hardware latency). The manual's example starts with pmlogger.service 32.875s, systemd-networkd-wait-online.service 20.905s, dev-vda1.device 13.299s.

systemd-analyze critical-chain prints the time-critical chain of units for the default target; '@' is the time the unit became active, '+' the time it took to start; the output can mislead because of socket activation and parallel execution. In the manual's example the chain ends at multi-user.target @47.820s and pmlogger.service is not on it.
On the manual's critical-chain example the '+' values sum to 29.247s (61.2% of 47.820s) and systemd-networkd-wait-online.service +20.905s is 71.5% of that sum and 43.7% of 47.820s.
claims.verified_by: Computed by the author with a short Python script on 2026-10-19.

claims.claim_vi: journalctl: -b shows the current boot, -b -1 the one before, --list-boots lists boots, -p filters by syslog priority (lower numbers are more important), -k shows kernel messages.

In the authoring container systemd-analyze blame fails with 'System has not been booted with systemd as init system (PID 1). Can't operate.', journalctl -b reports no journal files, systemd-analyze timespan '1min 9.608s' prints 69608000 microseconds, and systemd-analyze verify accepts a trivial unit file (systemd 255.4).

design_notes_vi: Bốn bước đánh số cho bốn lệnh, mỗi bước nêu số của ví dụ trong tài liệu, và một khung ghi nhớ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source lists eight boot steps from power-on to login; the lesson uses none of them and covers instead how to measure and read boot time with systemd-analyze and journalctl, from the systemd manual pages.
The eight steps themselves are covered by the other lesson of the same source (sd-08-020); this lesson links to it only through the related field.
